---

## How to read this

**The method is gone.** Every structural component of the dispatch-by deadline
— the round trip, the feasible-time computation, the latest-departure output,
the non-monotone safe-interval set, whole-traversal hazard, non-anticipative
information — is occupied, most of it by work that never mentions fire. SIPP
has represented alternating safe/unsafe intervals since 2011; Kamphuis has
reported a latest guaranteed departure time since 2022.

**That is not the end of the program.** Under `NOVELTY_STANDARD.md` §8 the
empirical and artifact axes are scored separately and an empirical
contribution is a legitimate scientific contribution. What no retrieved work
has done is *instantiate* these methods for an assisted wildfire evacuation
under a **modelled fire with quantified forecast error**, and report the result
for a real landscape.

**Two leaves remain above UNKNOWN**, and both are narrow:
- **WG-FV-3** — the tuned *positional trigger* comparator. Nobody found an
  occupant; Ardid tunes an *index threshold*, which is a different object.
- **WG-DBD-7 / the empirical axis of RQ2** — Korean village-scale dispatch-by
  *times*. `kim2011evacmap` occupies the Korean evacuation *map* since 2011,
  but emits routes, never a time.

**WG-COMB-1 is the one genuinely unexplored question, and we cannot yet say
so.** Its search reached only S1. Under §3.2 that supports nothing. Closing
that gap is the highest-value remaining search in the repository.
